lanes.label: Elsewhere in scripture
lanes.range: Topics in other books wired to this one

nodes.d: The burden of the word of the LORD to Israel by Malachi: a series of disputes in which the LORD states a charge, the people ask how, and he answers, ending with the coming day of the LORD and the promise to send Elijah.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Malachi's disputes work and how the book ends?

nodes.d: The LORD says he loved Israel, and when they ask how, he points to Jacob and Esau, saying he loved Jacob and hated Esau and laid waste Esau's mountains; he promises that he will be magnified from the border of Israel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how the LORD answers the question 'Wherein hast thou loved us?' in Malachi 1:2-3?
ev: Say what happens to Edom's plans (1:4)

nodes.t: Polluted offerings and a great name
nodes.d: The LORD rebukes priests who despise his name by bringing blind, lame and sick animals as offerings and call his table contemptible; he says he has no pleasure in them and that his name will be great among the Gentiles everywhere.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what was wrong with the offerings in Malachi 1 and what the LORD says about his name?
ev: Describe the offerings and the priests' attitude (1:7-8, 1:12-13)

nodes.d: The LORD sends a commandment to the priests: his covenant with Levi was of life and peace, and Levi feared him and turned many from iniquity, but the priests have departed from the way, caused many to stumble and been partial in the law.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} contrast Levi and the priests of Malachi's day in chapter 2?

nodes.d: Malachi charges Judah with profaning the covenant of the fathers and marrying the daughter of a strange god, and with dealing treacherously with the wife of their youth, since the LORD hates putting away; they also weary him by saying evildoers please him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the LORD condemns in Malachi 2:10-16?
ev: Say what wearies the LORD in 2:17

nodes.d: The LORD announces a messenger to prepare the way before him and the LORD coming suddenly to his temple, like a refiner's fire who purifies the sons of Levi; he will be a swift witness against sinners, for he does not change.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe who is coming in Malachi 3:1 and what he does in 3:2-3?

nodes.t: Return to me: tithes and offerings
nodes.d: The LORD tells the people to return, and when they ask how, says they have robbed him in tithes and offerings; he calls them to bring the whole tithe into the storehouse and promises to open the windows of heaven and rebuke the devourer.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD says about tithes and offerings in Malachi 3:7-12?

nodes.t: Is it vain to serve God?
nodes.d: The people say it is vain to serve God and call the proud happy; those who fear the LORD speak together and he writes a book of remembrance, and says they will be his jewels on the day he makes, spared as a son.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the book of remembrance in Malachi 3:16-17?
ev: Describe what the LORD does for those who fear him (3:16-17)

nodes.t: The day that burns; the Sun of righteousness; Elijah
nodes.d: The coming day burns the wicked like stubble, but for those who fear the LORD the Sun of righteousness arises with healing; the people are told to remember the law of Moses, and the LORD will send Elijah the prophet before the great day to turn hearts of fathers and children.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the two outcomes on the day of the LORD in Malachi 4 and what the LORD promises to send?
ev: Read the closing command and promise (4:4-6)

nodes.d: The gospel of Matthew, from the genealogy of Jesus Christ, son of David and son of Abraham (1:1), through the five great discourses, the passion and the resurrection, to the closing commission (28:16-20).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what Matthew is about and how it begins and ends?
ev: Describe the movement of the book: birth and preparation (1-4), the Sermon on the Mount (5-7), miracles and mission (8-12), parables of the kingdom (13), teaching on the way to Jerusalem (14-23), the coming kingdom (24-25), the passion and resurrection (26-28)
Name where the book starts and ends

nodes.t: John’s question and Jesus’ witness to John
nodes.d: John in prison sends disciples to ask whether Jesus is the one to come; Jesus points to the works done and then speaks of John as more than a prophet, the messenger of whom it is written “I send my messenger before thy face”, and of an unresponsive generation.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Jesus answered John’s question and what he said about John?
ev: Say what Jesus told John’s disciples to report

nodes.d: The gospel of Mark, from “the beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God” (1:1) through Jesus’ ministry in Galilee, the road to Jerusalem and his death, to the empty tomb and commission.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what Mark is about and where it begins and ends?
ev: Describe the movement of the book: John and the start of ministry (1), Galilee (1-8), the way to Jerusalem (8-10), the last week and passion (11-15), the empty tomb (16)
Say what Mark calls the book in 1:1

nodes.d: Mark opens with the beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God; John baptizes in the wilderness for repentance and says one mightier will baptize with the Holy Ghost.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain who John was and what he said about the one coming after him?
ev: Say how Mark begins his book

nodes.d: Luke writes an orderly account for Theophilus so he may know the certainty of what he was taught, from the births of John and Jesus to the resurrection, ascension and the apostles' commission.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Luke wrote his Gospel and where it begins and ends?
ev: Say who Luke addresses, why he wrote, and how the book begins and ends.

nodes.d: John in prison sends two disciples to ask whether Jesus is the one to come; Jesus points to the healings and the gospel preached to the poor, then calls John more than a prophet, the messenger sent before him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Jesus answered John's question and what he said about John?
ev: Say how Jesus answered John's disciples and what he said about John.

nodes.d: Paul's letter to the Romans, from the greeting and the gospel theme (1:1-17) to its closing greetings and doxology (16:27).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what Romans is about, using 1:16-17?
ev: Describe the movement: sin (1-3), justification (3-5), life in Christ and the Spirit (6-8), Israel (9-11), Christian living (12-16)

nodes.d: Paul answers the question of Israel by pointing to God's sovereign choice, from Isaac and Jacob onward, and his mercy.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Romans 9 says about God's choice and mercy?
ev: Link 9:7 to Genesis 21:12 and 9:12 to Genesis 25:23
